chunks: From him (Al-Fayyaz), he said: Hamdawayh narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and a man asked him about a man whom the prayer time overtakes while he is wading in water and cannot reach the ground. He (AS) said: 'If he is in war or in the path of Allah, let him pray by nodding (with his head). And if he is in trade, it was not appropriate for him to wade in the water until he prays.'
I said: 'And how should he do it?' He said: 'He should make it up (perform Qada) when he exits the water, having missed it.'

key_terms.ضَيَّعَهَا: Missed it / Failed to perform on time

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying while wading in water if prayer time passes?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between necessity (*darura*) and negligence (*taqsir*) in prayer obligations. It establishes that while war or travel permits performing prayer by nodding (*i'ima*) while wading, those in trade who delay prayer unnecessarily must make it up as a missed prayer, reflecting the balance between ease and diligence in Shia fiqh.
